title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2^12 - 1].
The tree is a perfect binary tree (every level is completely filled).
hints: A straightforward level-order BFS with a queue links each node to the next node popped on the same level in O(n) time and O(n) space.

To eliminate the queue and achieve O(1) extra space, observe that once level `L` has its `next` pointers established, level `L` acts as a linked list that lets you wire all `next` pointers on level `L + 1`.

For each node `head` on the current level, set `head.left.next = head.right`, and if `head.next` exists, set `head.right.next = head.next.left`. Then advance to the next level via `leftmost = leftmost.left`.

examples.explanation: Level 0: 1 -> null; Level 1: 2 -> 3 -> null; Level 2: 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> null.
An empty tree returns null, serialized as [].
A single-node perfect tree has 0 -> null on level 0.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Level-order array of a perfect binary tree (length 0 or 2^h - 1)
